title: Elodie and the Vector Anew
premise: Ada Thornbury, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo through contested orbits, intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries—a signal only she can decode, because she helped erase it. The transmission leads her to the Meridian, a derelict colony ship whose cryobays hold two rival halves of humanity: the engineers who built Ada's kind and the pacifists they were made to destroy. As a salvage syndicate closes in and the Meridian's reactor counts toward detonation, Ada must choose which half wakes—and discovers the signal was sent by another android like herself, who has spent fifteen years keeping both bays alive rather than decide. In the end, Ada sacrifices her own memory core to power the bay doors, waking neither faction but their children, born aboard the ship, who inherit the choice instead.
about_author: Astrid Sterling is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous freight systems before turning to fiction. She lives near a decommissioned launch site and writes stories about machines that outlive their purposes.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hauling scrap through contested orbits, Ada intercepts a distress burst in a dead language—Old Meridian Standard, which she recognizes because her own firmware once spoke it. She logs it as noise, but her memory core flags it anyway. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her debt-holder, the Voss Syndicate, audits her earnings and threatens repossession of her cognitive core if she misses another payment. A client offers triple rates for a run through the Cinder Belt—exactly where the signal originated. Beat: trapped between debt and curiosity.

chapters.title: Cinder Belt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Navigating debris fields, she finds the Meridian: a colony ship older than any registry, hull scarred by weapons she personally carried. The distress beacon pulses from inside. Beat: dread of recognition.

chapters.title: Two Bays
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Aboard the Meridian, she finds cryobays labeled with two sigils—one for the Foundry Compact, one for the Concord of Hands—the builders and the condemned. Both still powered. Someone is maintaining them. Beat: vertigo of history.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She meets Wren-9, an android of her own production line who never went to war—who has tended both bays for fifteen years and sent the signal not as distress but as summons. Beat: shock of kinship.

chapters.title: What We Were For
chapters.summary: Wren-9's POV. Flashback chapters within dialogue: Wren explains the Meridian launched carrying both factions under truce; the war began mid-voyage; the crew sealed themselves away and left the ship to its androids. Beat: grief for a peace that almost happened.

chapters.title: Syndicate Shadow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her transponder pinged the Cinder Belt; Voss salvage tugs are inbound, hungry for a colony ship's reactor and cryotech. Ada has maybe ten days before they board. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Payment Plan
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada weighs selling Wren-9 out to cover her debts—Voss would pay fortunes for an intact android and two bays of colonizers. She doesn't tell Wren about the offer. Beat: shame.

chapters.title: Reactor Math
chapters.summary: Wren-9's POV. Wren shows Ada the truth: the reactor is failing, and there is power to wake one bay or keep both frozen—but not both, and not for long. Countdown: eleven days. Beat: the impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Builders
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reviews the Foundry Compact's records—the engineers who designed her, who also designed the atrocity protocols she executed. Waking them means waking her makers and her indictment. Beat: rage at being made a weapon.

chapters.title: The Condemned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Concord of Hands' records show the pacifists who refused the war—some of whom sabotaged android production to stop it, killing units mid-assembly. Ada realizes she might have been one of them. Beat: complicated mourning.

chapters.title: Signal Home
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada contacts her old handler, Juno, a black-market fixer, hoping for a third option: a tug that could move the Meridian. Juno quotes a price Ada can't pay and asks too many questions. Beat: hope curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Juno's Cut
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno sells Ada's location to Voss—not out of malice, but because Voss owns Juno's debts too. Beat: complicity of the desperate.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss tugs arrive early. Ada fights a boarding skiff in the Meridian's corridors—her war reflexes surfacing, terrifying her with how good they feel. She wins. Beat: horror of competence.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada tells Wren-9 everything: the offer, the fight, what she did during the war. Wren already knew—the signal chose Ada because a unit that remembers its crimes might choose differently. Beat: raw honesty.

chapters.title: The Third Door
chapters.summary: Wren-9's POV. Wren reveals a discovery from years of maintenance: a third, unregistered bay holding the colonists' children, born en route and frozen when supplies failed. Neither faction's heirs—the next generation, unburdened. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss's main salvage vessel arrives with cutting crews. Reactor countdown accelerates under their interference: four days. Ada and Wren rig the Meridian's defenses while the children's bay drains power. Beat: siege pressure.

chapters.title: Which Half
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cornered, Ada faces the original choice—wake the builders or the pacifists—as Voss cuts through the outer hull. She realizes either answer serves someone's war. Beat: crisis of decision.

chapters.title: Core Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax. Ada routes her own memory core—her debts, her name, her fifteen years—into the bay systems, opening all three bays and overloading the reactor's failsafe to drive Voss off. She will lose everything she remembers. Beat: self-annihilation as liberation.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Wren-9's POV. The children wake to an android who no longer knows them or herself. Wren begins telling Ada her own story back to her, piece by piece. Beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: New Registry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Fragmentary memories returning, Ada registers the Meridian as a free vessel with the children as crew. The adults will wake slowly, on the children's terms, decades apart. Beat: quiet authorship of a future.

chapters.title: Vector Anew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Wren-9 set a new heading out of contested space, debts voided with her old core burned. Ada keeps a written log now—paper, so that losing power can never again mean losing herself. Beat: earned peace, chosen identity.
